newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers tackle issues from America to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers tackle issues from America to Zaire.

text.p: European Union Foreign Ministers meet in Luxembourg on Monday to tackle relations with countries spanning the alphabet -- from America to Zaire.

But while this diversity shows how far the EU has gone towards becoming a significant force on the international stage, the first issue of the day highlights how internal divisions threaten hopes for more common foreign policy from the bloc.

Commission hopes for approval for its proposals for tactics to counter Washington's Helms-Burton Act -- which seeks to outlaw trade with Cuba -- were quashed earlier this week when Denmark said it would veto the issue (see FOREIGN-CUBA).

But there are high hopes for unanimity on Zaire, which emerged as the latest trouble spot in Africa's Great Lakes region following clashes between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsis in the east of the country.

Ministers are to do discuss a Belgian proposal to appoint a special European envoy specifically to promote and encourage democracy in the vast central Africa nation -- which it ruled for years as a colonial power.
Ministers will also discuss the possibility of emergency aid for some 300,000 refugees from Rwanda and Burundi caught in the fighting .
Monday will also see the EU sign a Framework Agreement with South Korea, the first step towards strengthening potentially lucrative trade ties.

Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan is also due to report on progress being made towards working on a common position to be adopted by the bloc at the World Trade Organisation ministerial meeting in Singapore in December.
Ministers will also hear a report on the European Monitoring Centre for Racism and Xenophobia -- an issue the bloc is keen to tackle.
Other issues to be tackled include relations with former Yugoslavia, the inter-governmental conference, a cooperation council with Egypt and the Middle east peace process.
